slides.title: Systems with no solution: ==free points== you're leaving behind
slides.hand: 30 seconds each once you see it

slides.title: No solution
slides.body: No solution means parallel lines: same slope, different intercepts. Match the slopes, check the intercepts differ. That is the whole problem.

slides.title: Infinitely many solutions
slides.body: Infinitely many means both equations are the same line. One is just the other multiplied by a number — and every term must scale, including the constant.

slides.stem: `3x + 6y = 12` and `x + 2y = k` have infinitely many solutions. What is k?
slides.prompt: There's a lazy-match trap here. Comment your answer.

slides.title: B — 4
slides.body: Divide the first equation by 3 and you get `x + 2y = 4`, so k = 4. If you picked 12, you copied the constant without dividing it too.
